messages:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - GPU node provisioning failures for cluster 'prod-gpu' (queue growth > 1200). Autoscaler failing to create nodes. Pager link: https://pager.company/incident/INC-5421 :rotating_light:
jamie: oncall here, looking now. What region?
matt: eu-west-1, metric spike started ~10m ago. Grafana: https://grafana.company/d/abc/prod-gpu-queue (requests in queue -> 1.2k).
diego: seeing a bunch of ClusterAutoscaler errors in logs: `Failed to describe launch template version: UnauthorizedOperation` and `ASG update failed: InstanceProfileNotFound`
sarah: I can pull autoscaler logs, past 5m filter: `scale-up: could not create nodegroup: LaunchTemplateVersionMismatch`
jamie: tagging this as P1. @alex can you confirm any recent launch-template or IAM changes?
alex: I pushed a new launch template version this morning to add subnet changes, but didn't touch instance profile. Checking.
infra-bot: Deploy job #4501 applied lt: prod-gpu-launchtemplate v12 -> v13 at 07:24 UTC. No instance profile edits recorded.
matt: cluster-autoscaler logs: ```I0427 07:34:12 main.go:213] Failed to create instance: error creating launch configuration: UnauthorizedOperation: You are not authorized to perform this operation. status code: 403, request id: ...```
diego: AWS console shows ASG `prod-gpu-asg` stuck at desired=0 min=0 max=12, recent scaling attempt hit API throttling (RateLimitExceeded) and then `AttachInstanceProfile` call returns `NoSuchEntity` for instance profile arn:aws:iam::123456789:instance-profile/prod-gpu-ec2-role
jamie: so two separate failure classes: 1) 403/unauthorized for LT create, 2) instance profile missing when attaching. Which explains nodes not provisioning and pods piling in pending.
sarah: customer impact: `/v1/generate` p50 latency skyrocketed from 180ms -> 3.3s; error rate for generation requests increased from 0.2% -> 6% in last 12m. CS ticket queue increasing. @cs-rep FYI.
cs-rep: already getting inbound from two enterprise customers, they see timeouts. Not yet SLO breach but trending fast.
alex: digging IAM logs... I see an automation job removed the instance-profile resource earlier as part of cleanup (PR #382) — that seems accidental. Recreating it now.
diego: in the meantime the autoscaler keeps trying and getting launchtemplate mismatch because the default launch template version referenced by the ASG is v12 while CA attempts v13 -> mismatch path. CA logs: `LaunchTemplate version is not in the allowed set`
jamie: mitigation plan: 1) recreate instance profile and attach to LT/ASG 2) temporarily set ASG max=24 to avoid hitting scale ceiling 3) create an emergency fallback nodegroup with older LT version and looser taints so scheduler can place critical pods 4) throttle noncritical batch jobs (move to spot pool) 5) update incident channel when each step completes.
matt: I'm on (1). recreating instance-profile `prod-gpu-ec2-role` with same policies from backup.
alex: PR rollbacks disabled, doing manual attach. Watch for `AttachInstanceProfile` success.
(3 minutes pass)
matt: instance profile recreated and attached to instance profile name `prod-gpu-ec2-role`. AWS console shows success.
diego: autoscaler logs show fewer 403s but now: `ASG capacity error: RequestLimitExceeded` and some nodes still failing because LT version mismatch.
jamie: (2) I'm increasing ASG max to 24 now to allow scale-up. Doing it via console so automation doesn't overwrite.
alex: done, ASG max=24, desired still 0 because LT failing.
sarah: starting manual creation of emergency nodegroup: using LT v12 (last known-good), tolerations: `gpu-emergency:NoSchedule` removed, instanceType=g5.4xlarge, count=4.
matt: creating nodegroup `gpu-emergency-fallback-1` now with user-data that matches kubelet registration.
infra-bot: Nodegroup creation initiated -> nodegroup id ng-emer-20270427.
(5 minutes)
infra-bot: Nodegroup `gpu-emergency-fallback-1` reports 3/4 instances in service, 1 provisioning.
diego: scheduler is placing some pods on the emergency nodes. Pending pods dropped from 1200 -> 460. Queue throughput improving.
sarah: throttling lower-priority batch routes via feature flag: `ff.batch-fallback` -> true. Will reduce enqueue by about 60%.
jamie: good. Are any customer-facing endpoints returning 500s?
sarah: some `502` from our edge caches while upstream times out, but errors are falling. p95 latency for generate down to 1.4s from 3.3s.
cs-rep: telling customers we have mitigation in place and ETA ~20m to restore.
matt: autoscaler now shows successful LaunchTemplate describe and ASG attach working. Scaling events triggered: +4 nodes.
diego: CA log: `ScaleUp: No issues launching instances. Node additions accepted.`
(10 minutes)
jamie: handoff: I'm still oncall but handing to matt for follow-up while I eat. matt do you accept?
matt: accepting handoff. I'll stay and coordinate with infra team for follow-ups.
jamie: thanks. Updated incident status: MITIGATED (emergency nodegroup + ASG fix).
sarah: customer impact summary for postmortem: - duration of elevated queue: ~18m - peak pending pods: 1.2k - impacted endpoint: /v1/generate - estimated affected requests: ~14k - visible errors: 6% error rate peak - enterprise customers notified.
alex: root cause preliminary: automation job removed instance-profile during a cleanup run; launch template version rollout created mismatch between CA and ASG; combined with ASG max that was too low and API rate limits throttling creates the cascade.
matt: follow-ups (action items): 1) Restore instance-profile protection in infra automation (PR to lock) 2) Add validation to LT rollout to ensure CA/ASG reference versions 3) Add grace scale buffer: ASG max padding + emergency fallback nodegroup pre-warmed for burst 4) Add playbook steps for manual create fallback nodegroup 5) Update SLO runbook to notify CS earlier.
jamie: agreed. tagging infra and platform for owners.
cs-rep: customers ack'd mitigation notes, will follow up for RCA.
(incident-bot): Incident CLOSED (mitigated) - duration 1h 2m - file postmortem: https://wiki.company/INC-5421-postmortem
jamie: thanks team. I'll file the postmortem and assign follow-ups. Closing thread.
